channel.title: Mozilla Corporation — recent CVEs
channel.description: Most recent CVEs assigned by Mozilla Corporation (mozilla).

item.title: CVE-2026-126136 — OAuth2 access token could be sent over an unencrypted connection with Exchange accounts
item.description: For Exchange accounts using EWS or Microsoft Graph with OAuth2 authentication, Thunderbird sent the OAuth2 access token to the server even when the configured server URL used unencrypted HTTP. An attacker able to observe network traffic could obtain…

item.title: CVE-2026-126135 — SMTP and POP3 response injection when using STARTTLS
item.description: If an attacker was able to perform a man-in-the-middle attack on an SMTP or POP3 server connection using STARTTLS, the attacker could inject server responses before the TLS handshake completed. Thunderbird would process these responses after the hand…

item.title: CVE-2026-126134 — Feed subscriptions could leak NTLM credentials on Windows
item.description: Thunderbird allowed feed subscriptions to file: URLs that point to a network share. If a user was tricked into subscribing to such a URL, Thunderbird connected to the attacker's server when fetching the feed. Windows then sent the user's NTLM credent…

item.title: CVE-2026-126133 — Calendar server credentials could be sent to an HTTP proxy
item.description: When a CalDAV or ICS calendar was accessed through an HTTP proxy that requested authentication, Thunderbird could answer the proxy with the calendar server's username and password. This affected both setting up a new calendar and syncing existing cal…

item.title: CVE-2026-126132 — Attachments could be replaced with local file content when forwarding
item.description: When a message was forwarded inline, edited as new, or had an attachment dragged into a compose window, a specially crafted link attachment (a .desktop file on Linux, or a .url or .lnk file on Windows) was replaced with the content of the file or URL…
